svg.title: On the reflecting plane the reflected pulse is Ft,bc 7→εbεcFt,bc, where εa = −1 and all other εb = 1. Substitute these signs into the bilinear Maxwell stress. Its normal-normal component is P −1 b,c ∥Ft,bc∥2. The mixed terms with exactly one normal index change sign; skew symmetry 2 gives Ft,aa = 0, and combining the remaining terms yields exactly this negative half-sum. Integrate its divergence over the positive half-box, removing small balls about its finitely many upper sources. The plane term has the negative outward normal; the small-sphere terms are the translation case of the pulse-current identity (FS2). The reflected sources are in the negative half-space and cause no extra sphere term. The other box faces disappear as their size tends to infinity. Indeed each pulse of order d is O(|y|−4−d); its bilinear stress is O(|y|−8−di−dj), while the three-dimensional face measure is O(R3). Their fluxes are therefore O(R−5−di−dj).
